Sarah — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. High level answers below and I attached a short options packet that maps cost and SLA tradeoffs.

Short answers:
- Archival vs live: archived retrievals are billed from a separate credit bucket (archival-replay credits) and have a different SLA (targeted 95th p95 retrieval within 60s for the 12-month slab). Live retention/trace (hot) consumes the live retention credits and impacts token/ingest billing as usual.
- Pilot path: yes — we typically do a 90-day pilot that includes a small committed archival slab (example: 1TB/month) + dashboard seats. During the pilot we enable accelerated retrieval for a bounded number of replay requests.
- Onboarding migration credits: we can provide a one-time migration credit (applied as archival credits) to shorten the delta and cover bulk ingestion during onboarding.

Three packaging options (summary):
1) Pay-as-you-go: No commit, archival-replay credits consumed per retrieval; dashboard seats billed monthly. Best for discovery; higher unit price on retrievals.
2) 12-month commit (recommended for BrightPort): Commit to a retention slab (e.g., 3TB/month) — lower per-GB archival rate, includes an annual allotment of migration credits and discounted dashboard seat pricing. SLA: 99% uptime on dashboard and p95 retrieval within 45s for committed slabs.
3) Hybrid pilot -> scale: 3-month pilot (small commit) with conditional credits that convert into a 12-month contract at NTE pricing. Pilot includes 10k migration credits and 2 dashboard pro seats.

I attached a 2-page PDF with numbers and an outline for the pilot scope. If you want, Ben can run a short TCO model for your 8TB footprint.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm if procurement needs us to include standard SOC 2 language in the SOW (Kim will help).
- If pilot looks good, I’ll send a pilot SOW + a DocuSign link to accept the one-time migration credit structure.

Thanks,

- Migration credit mapping: pilot example (10,000 migration credits) ~= 2.5TB of cold ingest (after typical compression/encoding) — we’ll provide a compact worksheet to map your exact profile. Ben will run the TCO with your 8TB numbers and share by EOD tomorrow.

- Encryption/KMS: yes — archived traces can be encrypted with your AWS KMS CMK in Private deployments or via our VPC key integration for Dedicated. We’ll include explicit KMS clauses in the SOW.

If BrightPort signs a 12-month commit at >= 3TB/month within 30 days, Redwood will: 
- Provide a one-time migration credit equal to 5TB of ingest (applied as archival credits),
- Provide a 50% discount on the first quarter of dashboard seats during onboarding,
- Include an SLA appendix guaranteeing p95 replay <45s for the committed slab.

I’m attaching the pilot SOW draft and the DocuSign envelope for the pilot acceptance. If procurement is OK with the conditional concession we’ll mark the HubSpot deal as committed and route legal for a standard SOW with the KMS appendix.
